chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Hanaan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I was with him upon the food-spread, so he gave me a radish and said: 'O Hanaan! Eat the radish, for therein are three qualities – its leaf dispels the wind, and its core eases the flow of urine, and its root cuts the phlegm'. And in another report: 'And its leaf nourishes'.
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of radish according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the Shia tradition of integrating practical medicine with spiritual guidance, emphasizing the radish's specific therapeutic properties for digestive and urinary health. The mention of 'fujlah' (often identified as radish or turnip) reflects the empirical medical knowledge of the Imams, while the variant reading regarding the leaf's nourishing quality highlights the nuanced transmission of prophetic traditions within Shia scholarship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Hanaan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and I was with him<sup>asws</sup> upon the food-spread, so he<sup>asws</sup> gave me a radish and said: ‘O Hanaan! Eat the radish for therein are three qualities – its leaf dispels the wind, and its core eases the flow of urine, and its root cuts the phlegm’.
And in another report: ‘And its leaf nourishes’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar from his father from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadaniy from Hanan who has said the following: “

I once heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying; when I was with him at the table of food, he gave me a piece of radish and said, ‘O Hanan, you must eat radish because there are three qualities in it; its leaves repel gas, its essence quickens urine, and its root cuts off phlegm.’ In another Hadith it is said that its leaves make it pleasant.”
